sentences.en: From NPR, this is Hidden Brain.
Let's say you're invited out to eat at a gourmet restaurant.
sentences.zh: 假设你受邀去一家高级餐厅吃饭。

sentences.en: Your host has promised to cover the bill.
What do you decide to order?
This scenario unfolds in an episode of the TV show, The Office.
sentences.zh: 这个场景出现在电视剧《办公室》的一集里。

sentences.en: One of the characters, Jim, needs a favor from his colleagues, Phyllis and Stanley.
sentences.zh: 其中一个角色吉姆需要同事菲莉丝和斯坦利帮个忙。

sentences.en: So he takes them out to lunch on his dime.
sentences.zh: 所以他自掏腰包请他们吃午饭。

sentences.en: I'll have the surf and turf with a side order of lobster.
sentences.zh: 我要海陆大餐，再单点一份龙虾。

sentences.en: Actually, the surf and turf does come with lobster.
sentences.zh: 事实上，海陆大餐本身就包含龙虾。

sentences.en: Call it the surf and turf conundrum.
sentences.zh: 不妨称之为海陆大餐难题。

sentences.en: If you're paying for your own meal, you might choose the soup and salad.
sentences.zh: 如果是自己买单，你可能会选择汤和沙拉。

sentences.en: But if someone else is paying?
How much wine do you have?
It's tempting to ask for a lot more.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易忍不住点更多。

sentences.en: There's a hidden problem with choosing the surf and turf and the side of lobster.
sentences.zh: 选择海陆大餐和单点龙虾背后隐藏着一个问题。

sentences.en: If everyone at the table does this, your host can end up broke and resentful.
sentences.zh: 如果桌上的每个人都这么做，请客的人最后可能会破产且满腹怨言。

sentences.en: It might be the last time you get asked out to eat.
sentences.zh: 这可能是你最后一次被邀请出去吃饭了。

sentences.en: Now consider the surf and turf conundrum in a different context.
sentences.zh: 现在我们在不同的语境下思考海陆大餐难题。

sentences.en: What happens when we look not at a restaurant, but in a hospital?
sentences.zh: 如果我们看的不是餐厅，而是医院，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Many people, I think, are under the mistaken impression that they're not really paying for health care because the insurance company is paying for health care.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多人有一种错误的印象，觉得他们并没有真正在为医疗保健付费，因为保险公司在付钱。

sentences.en: And as a result, I think one of the culprits in our health care crisis right now is the behavior of us individually as patients.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为当前医疗危机罪魁祸首之一，是我们作为病人的个体行为。

sentences.en: That we do tend to expect that more action is better.
sentences.zh: 我们往往期望采取更多的行动越好。

sentences.en: There's no free lunch in health care.
sentences.zh: 医疗保健没有免费的午餐。

sentences.en: The individual choices we make as patients, doctors, and insurers might seem rational, but they are producing outcomes that are worse for everyone.
sentences.zh: 作为患者、医生和保险公司，我们做出的个人选择看起来可能很理性，但它们产生的结果对每个人来说都更糟。

sentences.en: How to fix the problem using economics and psychology, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 如何用经济学和心理学来解决这个问题，本周的Hidden Brain。

sentences.en: Vivian Lee is the author of The Long Fix, solving America's health care crisis with strategies that work for everyone.
sentences.zh: 维维安·李是《彻底修复：用对每个人都有效的策略解决美国医疗危机》一书的作者。

sentences.en: She's also president of Health Platforms at Verily Life Sciences and is a senior lecturer at Harvard Medical School.
sentences.zh: 她还是Verily生命科学公司健康平台总裁，也是哈佛医学院的高级讲师。

sentences.en: Vivian Lee, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 维维安·李，欢迎来到Hidden Brain。

sentences.en: Some years ago, you were heading up the University of Utah Health System and you had a patient on Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 几年前，你曾领导犹他大学医疗系统，当时你有一位医疗白卡患者。

sentences.en: In the past year, she had come into the emergency room 52 times.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，她去了52次急诊室。

sentences.en: What were the medical complaints that were bringing her in?
sentences.zh: 是什么医疗不适把她带到这里的？

sentences.en: They varied all over the place.
Sometimes she had some new issues that would come up.
sentences.zh: 有时她会出现一些新问题。

sentences.en: I think sometimes the staff just felt that she was lonely and had nowhere to go and wanted to drop by.
sentences.zh: 我想有时候工作人员只是觉得她很孤独，无处可去，所以想顺便过来坐坐。

sentences.en: And presumably, some of the visits that the ER was seeing this woman for were repeat visits.
sentences.zh: 想必，急诊室接待这位女士的一些就诊是重复就诊。

sentences.en: Did someone stop to say, hang on a second, why isn't this woman seeing a primary care doctor?
sentences.zh: 有没有人停下来问一句，等一下，为什么这位女士不去看初级保健医生？

sentences.en: Did Medicaid say, why isn't this woman seeing a primary care doctor instead of coming into the ER?
sentences.zh: 医疗白卡项目有没有说过，为什么这位女士不去看初级保健医生，而是来急诊室？

sentences.en: I'm sure many people thought about it.
sentences.zh: 我确信很多人都考虑过这个问题。

sentences.en: But, you know, emergency rooms are very busy places and they are, they're just hectic.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，急诊室非常忙碌，而且它们，它们就是很忙。

sentences.en: And while people may have had the idea, it wasn't really probably that easy to work out.
sentences.zh: 虽然人们可能有了这个想法，但可能真的没那么容易解决。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the key thing was to make sure that she was okay and to be able to discharge her out of the emergency room.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，关键是要确保她没事，并且能够让她出院离开急诊室。

sentences.en: So, something happened at the end of that year that fundamentally changed how you treated this patient.
sentences.zh: 因此，在那年底发生了一件事，从根本上改变了你对待这位患者的方式。
发生了什么？什么改变了？

sentences.en: Well, at the end of that year, the state of Utah announced that its Medicaid program would change radically.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在那年底，犹他州宣布其医疗白卡项目将发生根本性的改变。

sentences.en: So, leading up to that point, we were paid fee-for-service in our Medicaid program, which meant that every Medicaid patient, such as that woman who came in to our emergency room,
sentences.zh: 因此，在那之前，我们的医疗白卡项目采用按服务收费的付费方式，这意味着对于每一个医疗白卡患者，比如来到我们急诊室的那位女士，

sentences.en: we would charge for each visit, for every study that was performed, every medication that was prescribed or administered, for example.
sentences.zh: 我们会对每次就诊、执行的每一项检查、开具或施用的每一种药物收费，例如。

sentences.en: But at the end of that year, as of January 1st of the following year, we would get paid a fixed amount for caring for each of those Medicaid patients, such as this woman.
sentences.zh: 但在那年底，即次年1月1日起，我们将获得一笔固定金额，用于照顾每一个医疗白卡患者，比如这位女士。

sentences.en: And what that would mean is that if we ended up spending more than that allocated amount, let's say maybe $10,000 a year, for example, if we ended up spending more,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，如果我们最终的花费超过了分配的金额，比方说一年1万美元左右，如果我们最终的花费更多，

sentences.en: then that would be on our dime.
sentences.zh: 那么这就要我们自掏腰包了。

sentences.en: That would be a hit to our profit and loss statement.
sentences.zh: 这将对我们的损益表造成打击。

sentences.en: And so, it completely changed the way in which we started thinking about patients like her.
sentences.zh: 因此，它彻底改变了我们开始看待像她这样的患者的方式。

sentences.en: Before, she was a profit center.
sentences.zh: 以前，她是我们的利润中心。

sentences.en: Afterward, she was a cost center for us.
sentences.zh: 后来，她成了我们的成本中心。

sentences.en: What did you actually do that was different compared to what you were doing before?
sentences.zh: 与以前的做法相比，你实际上做了什么不同的事情？

sentences.en: Well, what was interesting about that change in the payment model was actually it enabled us to do what most of us felt was the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，付费模式的这种改变有趣的地方在于，它实际上使我们能够去做我们大多数人觉得是正确的事情。

sentences.en: So, this was the challenge, I think, that we had been facing up to that point,
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这是我们直到那时一直面临的挑战，

sentences.en: which was that our financial incentives really were in complete conflict with what our professional standards were.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们的财务激励与我们的职业标准完全冲突。

sentences.en: First, we collected a lot of data about all the patients on Medicaid who were coming through our system and identifying patients such as this woman.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们收集了通过我们系统的前往医疗白卡的所有患者的大量数据，并识别出像这位女士这样的患者。

sentences.en: And so, she was a big flag in the system because she had seen us 52 times in the previous year.
sentences.zh: 因此，她在系统中是一个巨大的红旗，因为她在前一年已经来看过我们52次了。

sentences.en: And then we all sat down and said, well, what should we be doing to care for a woman like this?
sentences.zh: 然后我们大家坐在一起说，好吧，为了照顾这样的女性，我们应该做些什么？

sentences.en: Well, she should be assigned to a primary care physician.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她应该被分配给一名初级保健医生。

sentences.en: We should make sure that she has access to transportation to come to and from clinic in case that might be a barrier.
sentences.zh: 我们应该确保她有交通工具往返诊所，以防交通是个障碍。

sentences.en: We should make sure she's able to refill her prescriptions as necessary.
sentences.zh: 我们应该确保她能够根据需要重新配药。

sentences.en: We really started to take care of her and focus on her health.
sentences.zh: 我们真正开始照顾她并关注她的健康。

sentences.en: So, embedded in the story is the central idea of your book.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个故事中蕴含着你书中的核心观点。

sentences.en: The United States has built a massive health care system where billing, payments, and the focus are on services provided rather than on outcomes.
sentences.zh: 美国建立了一个庞大的医疗系统，其账单、支付和重点都放在提供的服务上，而不是结果上。

sentences.en: You call it the fee-for-service monster.
sentences.zh: 你称之为按服务收费的怪兽。

sentences.en: Can you give me a sense of the scope and scale of the system that we have built?
sentences.zh: 你能让我了解一下我们建立的系统的范围和规模吗？

sentences.en: health care system now is a $3.5 trillion industry.
sentences.zh: 医疗系统现在是一个3.5万亿美元的产业。

sentences.en: It's consuming about 18% of the U.S.
And that's around two and a half to three times as much as our colleagues say in much of Europe, in Japan, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, and so on.
sentences.zh: 这大约是我们的同行在欧洲大部分地区、日本、澳大利亚、新西兰、加拿大等地的两倍半到三倍。

sentences.en: And yet, same time, our outcomes are significantly worse than most of those countries in terms of, for example, how long our babies are likely to live who are born today.
sentences.zh: 然而，与此同时，我们的结果明显比大多数国家差，例如，今天出生的婴儿可能能活多久。

sentences.en: So, even though we are spending so much money, we are not getting the results that we really deserve with that.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管我们花了这么多钱，但我们并没有真正得到应有的结果。

sentences.en: And that is a consequence of, in my view, the fee-for-service system or what I also call paying for action.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是按服务收费系统或我所谓的为行动付费的结果。

sentences.en: We're paying for action, but we're not really paying for results.
sentences.zh: 我们为行动付费，但我们并没有真正为结果付费。

sentences.en: How did the system come about in the first place, Vivian?
sentences.zh: 维维安，这个系统最初是怎么来的？

sentences.en: I think everyone's intentions were good in the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我想大家一开始的意图都是好的。

sentences.en: So, at the start, I'd say it really took off with Medicare.
sentences.zh: 所以，一开始，我想它确实是从医疗保险开始兴起的。

sentences.en: So, with a government-run program of health care for seniors.
sentences.zh: 也就是针对老年人的政府运营的医疗保健项目。

sentences.en: ...security program to provide hospital care, nursing home care, home nursing service, and outpatient treatment for those over 65.
sentences.zh: ...保障计划，为65岁以上的老人提供住院护理、疗养院护理、家庭护理服务和门诊治疗。

sentences.en: Medicare will become law on July 1st, 1966.
sentences.zh: 医疗保险将于1966年7月1日成为法律。

sentences.en: The Medicare program, the government basically paid hospitals for services that were rendered, and eventually also paid physicians for services that were rendered.
sentences.zh: 在医疗保险计划中，政府基本上是为提供的服务向医院付费，最终也为提供的服务向医生付费。

sentences.en: So, every time we saw a patient in the hospital or in a clinic, we would send a bill over, and then we'd get paid.
sentences.zh: 所以，每次我们在医院或诊所看病人，我们就会寄出账单，然后我们就会得到报酬。

sentences.en: And in the beginning, that was really a pretty small part of the national economy.
sentences.zh: 一开始，这确实是国民经济中相当小的一部分。

sentences.en: It was what you might expect at the start.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是意料之中的起点。

sentences.en: But if you set up an economic incentive like that, you naturally tend to want to increase, it's sort of, I guess, human nature, or at least it is in our society,
sentences.zh: 但如果你建立这样一种经济激励，你自然会想要增加，这某种程度上，我猜，是人性，或者至少在我们社会中是这样，

sentences.en: to try to generate more revenue.
And so, people began to focus on revenue-generating behaviors or revenue-generating services, which were, for example, operating rooms, cancer centers,
sentences.zh: 因此，人们开始关注产生收入的行为或产生收入的服务，例如手术室、癌症中心，
基本上是高端护理和医院。

sentences.en: And so, that's why over the, let's say, late 70s, most of the 80s and early 90s, every major urban area was littered with giant cranes building huge medical facilities.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在70年代末、整个80年代和90年代初，每个主要城市都散落着巨大的起重机，在建造巨大的医疗设施。

sentences.en: We called it, actually, a supply-generated demand.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们称之为供给创造需求。

sentences.en: And so, the more operating rooms you had, the more MRI machines you had, the more patients were referred to those systeMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，你拥有的手术室越多，你拥有的磁共振成像仪越多，被转诊到这些系统的患者就越多。

sentences.en: And so, you could just continue to generate more and more fees and more and more business and more and more profit, frankly.
sentences.zh: 因此，坦率地说，你可以不断产生越来越多的费用、越来越多的业务以及越来越多的利润。

sentences.en: So, let's look at some of the attributes of this fee-for-service monster in a little more detail.
sentences.zh: 因此，让我们更详细地看看这个按服务收费怪兽的一些属性。

sentences.en: One of the fundamental principles that you identify is that more care is always better, because more care means more services, and more services means more remuneration.
sentences.zh: 你确定的基本原则之一是，更多的护理总是更好的，因为更多的护理意味着更多的服务，而更多的服务意味着更多的报酬。

sentences.en: Well, in a fee-for-service system, that's really what you're rewarding.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在按服务收费的系统中，这确实是你所奖励的。
你正在奖励更多的服务。

sentences.en: You're rewarding people doing things to other people.
sentences.zh: 你是在奖励人们对其他人做事情。

sentences.en: And actually, in many cases, you're rewarding that regardless of whether it actually improves a person's health.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在许多情况下，无论它是否真正改善了一个人的健康，你都在为此提供奖励。

sentences.en: So, as long as you do a lot of procedures, as long as you poke and prod patients and do more colonoscopies or operations or administer expensive chemotherapeutic agents,
sentences.zh: 因此，只要你做了很多手术，只要你对患者进行探查并做更多的结肠镜检查、手术或使用昂贵的化学治疗药物，

sentences.en: the more you do to them, the more money you make.
sentences.zh: 你对他们做的越多，你赚的钱就越多。

sentences.en: And so, the assumptions are more care is better, more visits are better, more treatment is better.
sentences.zh: 所以，假设是更多的护理更好，更多的就诊更好，更多的治疗更好。

sentences.en: And ironically, it actually might suggest that less prevention is also better, because if you don't prevent problems from happening, you're going to have problems that arise,
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，它实际上可能暗示更少的预防也是更好的，因为如果你不阻止问题的发生，你就会遇到出现的问题，

sentences.en: and more people are going to come into health care facilities seeking services.
sentences.zh: 会有更多的人涌入医疗机构寻求服务。

sentences.en: I'm not necessarily saying that doctors want people to be sick,
sentences.zh: 我并不是说医生一定希望人们生病，

sentences.en: but the financial incentives of the system seem to be almost against prevention in favor of actually treating problems once they arise.
sentences.zh: 但该系统的财务激励似乎几乎与预防背道而驰，而是倾向于在问题出现后进行治疗。

sentences.en: The fee-for-service system really does create all kinds of unintended consequences and incentives, including what you've just described,
sentences.zh: 按服务收费系统确实会产生各种意想不到的后果和激励，包括你刚才描述的那些，

sentences.en: which is to favor procedures against prevention, favors specialty care at the expense of, say, primary care or generalists.
sentences.zh: 即倾向于程序而非预防，倾向于专业护理而牺牲初级保健或全科医生的利益。

sentences.en: This is one of the reasons why orthopedic surgeons or neurosurgeons or cardiac surgeons are among the most highly compensated physicians compared to, say,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么整形外科医生、神经外科医生或心脏外科医生是薪酬最高的医生之一，相比之下，

sentences.en: family medicine or pediatrics or, say, general internal medicine, these primary care physicians who spend most of their time counseling patients and helping to prevent disease,
sentences.zh: 家庭医学、儿科或普通内科，这些初级保健医生将大部分时间花在咨询患者和帮助预防疾病上，

sentences.en: you know, encouraging them to stop smoking, lose weight, focus on vaccinations, focus on healthy diets.
sentences.zh: 你知道，鼓励他们戒烟、减肥、关注疫苗接种、关注健康饮食。

sentences.en: None of those are really very profitable right now in a fee-for-for-service system.
sentences.zh: 在按服务收费的系统中，这些现在实际上都不是很有利可图。

sentences.en: And the ironic thing is, at the end of this, it's also antithetical to what patients want, because ultimately, if I was a patient,
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，最后，这也与患者想要的背道而驰，因为最终，如果我是一个病人，

sentences.en: what I really want is to be as healthy as possible with minimal contact with the health care system.
sentences.zh: 我真正想要的是尽可能保持健康，同时与医疗系统的接触最少。

sentences.en: Well, that may be true, but I think that that's an important issue that you raise, which is that, of course, if you ask most people, they want to be as healthy as possible,
sentences.zh: 好吧，这可能是真的，但我认为你提出了一个重要的问题，那就是，当然，如果你问大多数人，他们希望尽可能保持健康，

sentences.en: and they never really want to encounter a physician, at least unless perhaps if they're delivering a baby, for example, which is a moment of joy for most people.
sentences.zh: 他们真的永远不想去看医生，除非也许他们正在分娩，例如，对大多数人来说这是一个快乐的时刻。

sentences.en: But outside of that, most people don't.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，大多数人都不想。

sentences.en: However, I think it is also true that many patients, when they do encounter the health care system, there is a tendency to expect something to be done.
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为这也是事实，许多病人在接触医疗系统时，往往期望做点什么。

sentences.en: There's a tendency to feel like, well, if I've come to see you, I should at least walk out with a prescription or a referral to another physician or an imaging study, for example.
sentences.zh: 人们往往会觉得，好吧，既然我来看你了，我至少应该拿着处方、另一位医生的转诊单或影像学检查结果离开。

sentences.en: And one of the consequences of having an insurance-based health care system is that there is sort of this separation from who's actually paying versus who's actually getting the service.
sentences.zh: 拥有一个基于保险的医疗系统的后果之一，就是实际付费的人与实际获得服务的人之间存在着某种分离。

sentences.en: So many people, I think, are under the mistaken impression that they're not really paying for health care because the insurance company is paying for health care.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为许多人有一种错误的印象，觉得他们并没有真正在为医疗保健付费，因为保险公司在付钱。
